second_order: calling and joining attempts to draw a Haskell logo
theme_note: These passages call the room to draw, relaunch the attempt, or join because the shared template makes participation possible.

second_order: finding a spot away from the void and clashes
theme_note: These passages test threatened locations and answer by moving or choosing less-contested tiles; what varies is whether the danger is the void, an outdated script, or nearby claims.

second_order: keeping every pixel and the Haskell text repaired
theme_note: These passages rally defense, diagnose drift and entropy, recover pixels, or recast fighting as patient repeated placement.

These passages ask for, generate, limit, run, and update configurations; automation varies from protecting only priority text to accidentally undoing a newer shift and arriving after the canvas closed.

second_order: explaining r/place and welcoming people brought in by the logo
theme_note: These exchanges answer what the activity is, explain Haskell, and welcome a newcomer whose arrival makes the hoped-for recruitment visible.

second_order: redesigning the logo to read clearly in Haskell colors
theme_note: These passages propose, praise, measure, and complete changes to lettering, dimensions, expansion, and purple colors; participants vary over whether recoloring or expansion is worth the effort.

second_order: celebrating a place for Haskell and hoping it spreads
theme_note: These posts declare completion or success, thank contributors, and connect the visible mark to spreading Haskell and bringing in programmers.

second_order: handing the pixels to the community and opening a committee
theme_note: These passages pass maintainership to the community, open a proposal thread, and move active discussion to IRC when the decision venue changes.

second_order: making room when neighbours speak out
theme_note: These passages raise boundary harms, ask for peace or protection, and answer requests by limiting or abandoning expansion; the requests come from both Haskellers and visitors.

second_order: turning rivalry into jokes, threats, and score-settling
theme_note: These passages narrate programming-language takeover, threaten or mock griefing, claim post-event damage, and argue over priority and bots after placement ends.

second_order: working out whose nearby mark it is
theme_note: These passages report an unidentified encroaching figure, ask who owns a purple creature, make and retract a mistaken claim, and redirect the visitor to its owner.

second_order: announcing Haskell World News as the room own April Fools joke
theme_note: The announcement and Haskell Cafe pointer establish a separate community joke whose later Reddit reception can extend this practice without merging it into canvas work.

second_order: choosing how to waste effort on r/place
theme_note: This single code keeps the participant own framing of knowingly spending effort on the event; it does not share a practice closely enough with design, defense, or rivalry codes to force a merge.

second_order: locating and recognising the finished r/place spot
theme_note: After placement ends, these passages ask where the mark is, react to a linked glimpse, locate it by the Mona Lisa, and recognise it through a familiar Haskell slogan.
